archetype.name: Playoff Team (pass-first offense, middling defense)
archetype.definition: Baltimore is a top-five efficiency team whose record matches its play, built on Lamar Jackson's passing, with a defense that is average and leaks against the run.

report.headline: Lamar's arm is carrying a leaky run defense, and his ankle is the season
report.take:
Baltimore at 3-1 is a passing team that still calls plays like a running team. The offense ranks 4th in EPA per play, and almost all of that is the air game: 0.328 EPA per dropback (2nd) and a 50.2% success rate (2nd). The defense sits squarely in the middle at 15th. The +5 point differential per game (8th) and a near-zero 0.19 wins over expected say the record is honest. This isn't a team stealing close games. It's a good team with one elite unit. That unit outran a first-year staff that got a 2 preseason coaching grade, and a weapons room that has jumped from a 5 preseason grade to 9.7 now.

Jackson is the engine. He has 967 passing yards in four starts and has posted 10-plus passing EPA in three of four games. The protection is better than the old reputation: 13 QB hits allowed (3rd fewest) even though he holds the ball 3.11 seconds, the 2nd-longest time to throw in the league. The ground game tells a different story. Derrick Henry has taken 89 carries, but rushing EPA went from +6.7 and +3.0 in the first two games to -4.2 and -3.6 in the last two. The team still runs more than expected (pass rate over expected -5.1, 25th). The staff also goes for it on every fourth down it faces, yet ranks 31st in short-yardage conversion. That is aggression the run game hasn't earned.

The numbers hide two things. First, the schedule: the four defenses Baltimore has scored on now rank 22nd, 26th, 31st and 21st, so the offensive ceiling hasn't been tested by a good defense. Second, the defense is two different units. Pass defense is 9th, and against short throws it ranks 4th. But rushing EPA allowed is 27th, pressure rate is 27th and deep-ball EPA allowed is 19th. Points allowed (24 per game, 19th) run worse than yards allowed (317, 10th) because opponents score touchdowns on 64.3% of red-zone trips. Add 9.8 penalties a game (30th) and special teams at 25th, and you get a team that wins but rarely covers. It went 1-2-1 against the spread, losing outright as an 8.5-point favorite to New Orleans and drawing 131 penalty yards in a non-cover against Tennessee.

Where it goes depends on health. Jackson is questionable with an ankle and the coach openly doesn't know his chances. Starting guard Jovaughn Gwyn is on IR into December, center Ethan Pocic is on IR, Ronnie Stanley is questionable, and Trey Hendrickson is out on a defense already short on pressure. History says a healthy Jackson-led offense is real: it ranked 1st in 2024, a 12-5 year. Last year's 8-9 came with -2.8 wins over expected, a team that was unlucky rather than bad. With Jackson upright, this profiles as a double-digit-win division favorite. Without him, the thin defense has to carry far more than it has shown it can.

strengths.title: Elite, efficient Lamar passing game
strengths.body: Baltimore is 2nd in both dropback EPA and overall success rate, and Jackson has cleared 10 passing EPA in three of four games. The line protects him well despite his long time to throw, which lets him extend plays without taking hits. The 2024 history (offense 1st) says this is a real skill, not a hot streak. The caveat is that no above-average defense has tested it yet.

strengths.title: Pass defense smothers the short game
strengths.body: The defense ranks 9th in EPA allowed per dropback and 4th against short passes. Underneath completions go nowhere, which is why opponents have topped 252 passing yards only once. It holds up as long as the back seven stays healthy, though Marlon Humphrey's calf is a question mark. Deep balls (19th) are the leak.

strengths.title: Clean with the football
strengths.body: The offense has two giveaways in four games, with none in the last two, and the turnover margin of +0.8 per game ranks 5th. Some of this is sample size: five takeaways in four games is a pace that usually cools. Jackson's ball security behind a line that keeps him clean is the more durable part.

concerns.title: Jackson's ankle and a thinning line
concerns.body: Everything runs through Jackson, and his status for Atlanta is unknown. Tyler Huntley is the only other passer with yards this season. The interior is already patched: Gwyn, a 91%-snap starter, is on IR until December, and Pocic is on IR too. Left tackle Stanley and guard Vorhees are both questionable. If the protection that has kept Jackson clean breaks down, the offense loses the one thing that makes it elite.

concerns.title: Soft against the run, no pass rush
concerns.body: Baltimore ranks 27th in rushing EPA allowed and 27th in pressure rate, and misses tackles at the 22nd-worst rate. That means teams can run on it and quarterbacks get time to look deep. Losing Hendrickson to a finger fracture removes one of the few rushers on a unit with seven sacks. This is a structural flaw, not noise, and it is why the defense allows more points than its yardage suggests.

concerns.title: Penalties and special teams bleed margin
concerns.body: At 9.8 penalties per game (30th), five of them on the line (29th), plus special teams ranked 25th, Baltimore hands back hidden yardage every week. That is why a team ranked 5th in net EPA covers only a third of the time. It is fixable with coaching, but four games in, it has been consistent.

trend.note: Passing efficiency has held, with 10-plus EPA in three of four games after a Week 2 dip in the loss to New Orleans. Underneath that, the run game has gone negative in back-to-back weeks and winning margins have shrunk from +18 to +3 and +6.

nextGame.headline: Jackson's status decides it; Atlanta walls off the Henry run game
nextGame.body:
Atlanta is a strange matchup: the league's worst offense (32nd in EPA, 32nd passing) paired with a strong defense (8th) that is 1st against the run and 4th in pressure rate. That points Baltimore straight at what it does best. Throw it, don't feed Henry into the best run defense in football. Atlanta's rush rarely finishes, though: 27th in sack rate, with five sacks all season. A quarterback who extends plays can beat that pressure. On the other side, Atlanta's only working weapon is its run game (5th in rushing EPA, 2nd in yards per carry). That aims right at Baltimore's 27th-ranked run defense, and Atlanta's 2nd-ranked time of possession says it will try to grind. Atlanta's -2 turnover margin per game is the worst in the league, and that is Baltimore's cleanest path to separation.

Availability is the whole story. Jackson is questionable and his coach couldn't put odds on it. Stanley and Vorhees are questionable on a line that has already lost Gwyn and Pocic, Humphrey is questionable, and Hendrickson and Chris Moore are out. Atlanta has started three quarterbacks in three games (Cooper Rush, Tua Tagovailoa, Michael Penix Jr.), with Rush now the emergency QB. Its every-snap tackle Jake Matthews (groin) and edge Za'Darius Smith (concussion) are both questionable after leaving their last game. The short -2.5 line looks like a market pricing in real doubt about Jackson.

keyMatchups.title: Henry versus the league's best run defense
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta allows -0.312 EPA per rush, 1st by a wide margin, and ranks 2nd at preventing explosive runs. Baltimore's stuff rate is already 21st and its run EPA has been negative two weeks running. If Baltimore keeps running more than expected, it plays into Atlanta's hands. The right script is pass early.

keyMatchups.title: Atlanta pressure versus a patched interior
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta pressures at the 4th-highest rate, and Baltimore's quarterback holds the ball longer than almost anyone, now behind a reshuffled interior line. Atlanta's 27th-ranked sack rate says the pressure doesn't finish. Whether Baltimore's makeshift guards hold up is the pivot.

keyMatchups.title: Atlanta's ground game against a soft front
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta can't pass (-0.353 EPA per dropback, last) but runs efficiently, and Baltimore is 27th against the run without Hendrickson. If Atlanta stays on schedule on the ground, it shortens the game and keeps Baltimore's offense on the sideline. Forcing passing downs means forcing the league's worst passing attack to beat you.

nextGame.watch: Whether Jackson is active. If he is, watch whether Baltimore abandons the run against Atlanta's top-ranked run defense and puts the game on his arm early.

restOfSeason.body:
The passing efficiency is the sustainable part. It has history behind it (1st in offensive EPA in 2024), and the protection numbers support it. Expect the scoring pace to come down somewhat as the schedule stiffens with Cleveland, Cincinnati, Buffalo and Jacksonville in the next five weeks, after four soft defenses so far. The turnover margin will probably cool toward neutral. The run defense and pass rush look like genuine weaknesses rather than noise, and they get no help until Hendrickson returns. The penalty rate should drift down, since 30th is hard to stay at, which would help the cover rate more than the win column.

The back half is kind. Weeks 10-14 bring the Chargers, Houston and Tampa Bay (all 0-4) plus Carolina, and six division games remain against teams no better than 3-1. A healthy Jackson makes this a 10-12 win division favorite. An extended absence, layered on a line missing two interior players, drops it toward the 2025 version that slipped to 8-9.
swingFactors: Interior line health until Gwyn returns
Whether the run defense and pass rush stabilize

bets.lean: BAL -2.5 if Jackson is confirmed active
bets.reason: The short number prices in Jackson's uncertainty against a team with the league's worst offense and worst turnover margin. Baltimore's 5th-ranked net EPA should clear a field goal with him playing. Only play it after his status is confirmed, given Baltimore's 1-2-1 cover record and penalty habit.

Atlanta's games average 39.7 combined points. It holds the ball 2nd-most per game, runs well below expected pass rate, and fields an 8th-ranked defense. Baltimore's scoring came against defenses now ranked 21st-31st, and its run game is walking into the league's best run defense.
Atlanta is 1st in rushing EPA allowed, 3rd in success rate allowed and 2nd at preventing explosive runs. Henry's efficiency has already turned negative the last two weeks.

confidence.note: Four games against weak defenses, Jackson questionable, two interior linemen on IR.
